docs.title: Cobblemon Nuzlocke & Soul Link
docs.text:
A full Hardcore Nuzlocke the game enforces for you — one catch per zone, permadeath, mandatory nicknames, level caps — so you play the run instead of policing yourself. And if you play with friends, Soul Link ties your catches together: the Pokémon you caught in the same place live and die as one.

MC 1.21.1 Cobblemon 1.7.x Fabric NeoForge Requires Routes

The ruleset Soul Link

docs.title: 🎮 Hardcore Nuzlocke
docs.text: One catch per zone, permadeath you cannot heal your way out of, mandatory nicknames, level caps and a shiny clause. Works on a single-player world.

docs.title: ❤️‍🔥 Soul Link
docs.text: Catch in the same place as your partner and those two Pokémon are bound: one dies, both die. Two to four players. Optional.

docs.title: 🎓 Gym Leader Challenge
docs.text: One elemental type for the whole run — your starters are drawn from it, and your team may only carry it. Offered to each player at character creation.

docs.title: 🗺️ Trainers, gyms and a league
docs.text: Trainers along the roads, a gym beside every town, and the Elite Four out on a road as a place of its own.

docs.title: Installing
docs.text:
It is an add-on for Routes: the zones it locks onto are the routes, areas and towns Routes generates, so you need both. Get it from Modrinth or CurseForge, for Fabric or NeoForge on Minecraft 1.21.1.

Also needs Cobblemon 1.7.x (CurseForge) the Pokémon Architectury API (CurseForge) both loaders Cloth Config (CurseForge) the settings screen Fabric API (CurseForge) Fabric only

Trainers and level caps come from Radical Cobblemon Trainers (CurseForge) when it is installed; without it those features simply stand down.

docs.title: Zones come from Routes
docs.text:
The "one catch per zone" rule needs a definition of zone, and it takes it from Routes: the routes, areas and towns Routes generates are the capture zones. That is why this is an add-on rather than a mod with its own map model.

Not the Cobblemon Nuzlocke datapack

There is an unrelated datapack by RRULE2001 with a similar name. This is a different project — a mod — which is why this one carries Soul Link in its name.

docs.title: ⌨️ Commands & Config
docs.text:
Everything under the /nuzlocke root, and every switch the ruleset has. Routes' road commands live under /routes — the two never mix.

/nuzlocke

👤 status · log · map

🛡️ status player · reset · reviveenable · disable · set

soul link

👤 link · accept · decline · unlinkstatus · summary · parties

👤 = every player · 🛡️ = operator (permission level 2)

docs.title: Quick reference
docs.text: Command Who One-liner /nuzlocke status [player] 👤 / 🛡️ Zone records + party deaths ([player] is op-only). /nuzlocke log · key I 👤 The run's log — the Soul Link log while you are in a link. /nuzlocke map 👤 Dump your capture zones as map waypoints. /nuzlocke reset [player] 🛡️ Clear a player's zone records, lift their game-over and ask for a new Gym Leader Challenge type. They keep their team. /nuzlocke revive [player] [zone <zone>] 🛡️ Revive a party's dead Pokémon — all of them, or only the one caught in that zone (by the name the log shows). The mercy switch: it also lifts a game-over, and under Soul Link it revives each one's soulmates with it. /nuzlocke enable · disable 🛡️ Master switch for this world, saved per world. /nuzlocke config list 👤 Every setting for this world with its current value, by section. /nuzlocke config get <setting> 👤 Read one setting back. /nuzlocke config set <setting> <value> 🛡️ Change one, live. Offers the names and refuses a value out of range. /nuzlocke config reset <setting> 🛡️ Put one back to its default. /nuzlocke config reload 🛡️ Re-read config/cobblemon_nuzlocke.json, no restart needed. A world with its own settings keeps them. /nuzlocke config unoverride 🛡️ Drop this world's own settings, so it follows the config files again. /nuzlocke set <option> <value> 🛡️ The older spelling of config set, kept working. /nuzlocke debug exp 🛡️ Log what the level cap decides for each EXP gain. /nuzlocke soullink … 👤 The co-op suite — see Soul Link. /pokemonrestart 👤 Wipe your own run and start over. Its own command, not a /nuzlocke one — it belongs to the player whose run it is. Type it twice to confirm. It also takes you out of any Soul Link, forgets a trainer battle you walked away from, and offers the Gym Leader Challenge again when you pick your new starter.

docs.title: /nuzlocke soullink
docs.text:
Command What it does link <player2> [player3] [player4] Offers a contract. Nothing binds until everyone accepts. accept · decline Answer an offer. The prompt also appears as a screen you cannot dismiss. unlink Dissolves your binds. status Lists your binds in chat, with ✝ marking the dead. summary The linked-teams screen: every member's full party, soulmates marked ⇄. parties The same members, one party per player, offline members included.

Offering a link does not need the command — right-click a player and pick Soul Link from Cobblemon's interaction wheel.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
The ruleset is decided when you create the world, on a NUZLOCKE tab that sits next to GAME / WORLD / MORE. Installing this add-on is what adds that tab; Routes' own generation options live beside it on its ROUTES tab.

saved per world

live, same options

🆕 NUZLOCKE tabat world creation

🌍 Your world's rulesnever clobbered later

⚙️ /nuzlocke set option value

Choices are stored per world and applied to new worlds only, so loading an existing world never has its rules overwritten. Picking Hardcore at world creation turns the full ruleset on.

docs.title: 🎮 Hardcore Nuzlocke
docs.text:
The classic ruleset, enforced by the game instead of by your honour. Every rule below is a switch on the NUZLOCKE tab at world creation, and every one of them can be changed later — see Commands & Config. The one thing that is not a switch is the difficulty: while the ruleset is on, the world is set to Hard every time it starts.

docs.title: The rules
docs.text: Rule What it means 🎯 One catch per zone Only the first wild you meet in a zone is catchable. A spent zone bounces Poké Balls, in battle and out. Fleeing or knocking the encounter out spends it just the same. 💀 Permadeath A fainted Pokémon is dead: no healing of any kind, no battling, no trading. The PC or release, nothing else. ✍️ Mandatory nicknames A blocking screen on every Pokémon you obtain, showing its sprite, gender, ability and moves — so you name it knowing what it is. Leaving the game with the screen open brings it back on your next login, and you keep the Pokémon. Your starter is the exception: leave before naming it and the pick is undone, so you choose again from the same three. ✨ Shiny clause A wild shiny is always catchable and never spends the zone. 🔁 Duplicates clause A Pokémon whose line you already own cannot be caught, and does not spend the zone — that encounter waits for something new. What you own includes your starter, gifts, trades and everything you have evolved. 🥚 Egg clause A hatchling is tied to where it hatches, like a wild catch: it takes that zone's encounter, so an egg will not hatch in a zone you have already spent — it waits until you carry it somewhere new. This holds even with the first-encounter lock off, and a shiny hatchling spends the zone like any other. Eggs can also be banned outright, or exempted. 😴 Defeated Catch A wild you beat lies on the ground for a while, asleep at 1 HP and catchable — a second chance at the encounter, KO experience included. While it lies there it can only be caught, never battled again. 😠 Aggressive wilds About one species in five comes after you instead of meleeing you, and its first hit starts a battle. A wild above your level cap never does. 🏥 Whiteout Losing a battle sends you back to your respawn point: the last Pokémon Center you used, or your bed, or the world spawn without one. Running out of usable Pokémon anywhere is a Game Over. 📈 Level cap Follows your trainer card. Catches above it go straight to the PC, and no wild Pokémon above it turns a hit into a battle. 🎒 No bag in battle The battle bag is closed. A second mode blocks only healing, leaving X items legal — Poké Balls are never blocked.

docs.title: Zones
docs.text:
A zone is a place, and the place decides the rule. What counts as one place is your choice at world creation, under Capture zones are:

Mode A zone is Geography The world Routes draws: every numbered Area, every named route and every town is its own zone. A route's zone reaches one chunk past the road, so a Pokémon caught just off it counts for the route; where that strip touches two routes, the lower route number takes it. Everything not enclosed in an Area is one shared Wild zone, one per dimension — it is in your log from the first minute, and early on it is most of where you can catch, so growing the road network is what earns you new zones beside it. Biome The biome you are standing in. This is the classic tabletop rule, and the one that works from the first minute — it does not wait for a road network to exist. Both The pair. A route that crosses taiga and then swamp is two zones and gives you two encounters, listed as Route 3 — Taiga and Route 3 — Swamp.

Under Geography and Both, structures are sites, and a site grants one encounter per KIND of site: your first pillager outpost is an encounter, the next outpost is a place you have already spent. Site encounters can be switched off entirely, in which case a structure counts as whatever surrounds it.

Changing the mode part-way through a run re-reads every catch you have already made, which can re-open or merge zones you had spent. The setting says so where you pick it.

Crossing into a new zone puts its name on screen as a title, with its state beside it: ○ free, ● an encounter in progress, ✔ caught, ✘ lost. The title can be switched off.

docs.title: Zones a map maker drew
docs.text: A world builder can mark out their own towns, routes and areas with Routes' zone commands, and the run plays by them: walking into one announces the name they gave it, the one-catch rule covers that whole zone, and the log lists it under that name. Resizing or renaming a zone keeps the catch already made in it. Deleting one hands its ground back to the zones the generator drew.

docs.title: The log
docs.text: Press I (rebindable) for the run's record: every zone you have discovered, what you caught there, and whether it is still alive. Four chips across the top — Alive, Dead, Waiting, Empty — each say how many lines they stand for and turn that group off, so a long run can be read down to just the part you are after. Most of a long log is Empty: zones you have found and not yet had an encounter in. A second row filters by kind of zone — towns, routes, areas, sites, the Wild and your starter — and the two work together, so "the towns I have not caught in yet" is two clicks. Clicking a Pokémon's sprite opens its summary; one that is dead, released or in the PC says so instead. Your starter is in it, and so is anyone's Gym Leader Challenge type. In a Soul Link it becomes the link's log.

docs.title: 🎓 Gym Leader Challenge
docs.text:
One elemental type for the whole run. Your random starters are drawn from it, and you may only enter a battle while every Pokémon on your team carries it.

  • Each player is asked at character creation, and answers for themselves. Declining is one click. Server owners can switch the offer off for everyone.
  • An off-type catch still spends the zone. The challenge decides what you may use, not how many tries you get. Off-type Pokémon go to the PC.

docs.title: What it builds into the world
⚔️ Trainers on the roads
docs.text:
They challenge you on sight and duel each other between fights — but only when it is fair: you are not already battling, they are off cooldown, the levels are close, and you are in front of them. Nothing challenges you from behind. Crouching holds them off, so you can walk up and use the trainer's own menu, and so does riding over a drop with no ground to land on.

A trainer in a battle cannot be killed, so the fight always resolves. A trainer who has ended a run carries a ☠ tally of them in its name — and so does every other trainer of that name.

docs.title: 🏛️ A gym beside every town
docs.text:
Every town you discover gets its Gym Leader's gym next door, named after them. Leaders wait to be challenged — you walk in and ask. Lt. Surge is the exception.

Needs a pack that provides gym structures, such as COBBLEVERSE.

docs.title: 🏆 The Elite Four on a road
docs.text: One league per world, standing out on a route between settlements as a place of its own, with its own marker on the map. It has its own switch, apart from the gyms.

docs.title: 🌿 Pokémon on the roads
docs.text: Every road carries its own encounters: hidden sources set into the paving, each offering one family at its own level. See Route Pokémon.

docs.title: 🧗 The Escape Rope
docs.text: A one-tap trip back to your respawn point — and it will not fire mid-battle.

docs.title: 🌿 Route Pokémon
docs.text:
Every generated road carries encounter sources, disguised Cobblemon habitat blocks set into the paving. Each one offers one family of its own: the evolution stage that fits its level, and, when that stage is about to evolve, about one of the next stage for every three, five levels higher.

  • Most sources offer something native to where they stand: the biome on land, the sea or river under a water crossing. A source on a bridge deck leans toward Flying types instead.
  • Each source keeps its own number of Pokémon out, picked once from a range.
  • Now and then a source spawns an alpha, which counts as the zone's encounter like any other.
  • Now and then a source spawns an aggressive Pokémon, which comes after you on sight; its first hit starts a battle.
  • A route too short for the spacing still gets one source, halfway along.

Needs Cobblemon 1.8. Spacing, levels and odds are all settings — see Route Pokémon settings.

docs.title: 🧗 Escape Rope
docs.text:
Use it and you are whisked back to your respawn point, the same place a whiteout sends you.

Where it sends you the last Pokémon Center you used, or your bed or respawn anchor; the world spawn if you have none Restrictions Overworld only, never mid-battle, 10-second cooldown Cost one rope per use, free in creative

On a Nuzlocke run, refusing to fire mid-battle is the whole point: a fight you started is a fight you finish.

docs.title: 🪢 Crafting
docs.text:
A shapeless recipe — the arrangement in the grid does not matter, the ingredients just have to be in the table together. One craft makes two.

➜ 2 Ingredient Amount String 2 Ender Pearl 1 → Escape Rope 2

docs.title: Just want the routes?
docs.text: The whole ruleset stands down on demand and Routes keeps working — roads, waypoints and map paint all intact. Set Enable Nuzlocke to off on the NUZLOCKE tab at world creation, or run /nuzlocke disable on a world that already exists. To soften one rule instead of all of them, see Commands & Config.

docs.title: ❤️‍🔥 Soul Link (co-op)
docs.text: The cooperative Nuzlocke: two to four players sign a contract, and from then on the Pokémon they caught in the same place are bound to each other. One dies, they all die.

docs.title: The bind is where you caught it
docs.text:
Not a party slot, not the order you caught things in — the zone. You and your partner both catch something on Route 3, and those two Pokémon are soulmates for the rest of the run.

Every Pokémon in a linked run must be bound; pending is the only legitimate exception. An unbound Pokémon is one whose death would cost the group nothing, which is the one thing a Soul Link is.

Your starter counts as its own shared zone, so starters bind to starters. Gifts, trades and anything else you did not catch in the world share that same zone.

docs.title: 🔗 Bound
docs.text: Two or more members have caught in that zone. The Pokémon are tied together and free to battle.

docs.title: ⏳ Pending
docs.text: You caught somewhere your partner has not reached yet. It cannot battle until they catch there too — the chat tells you which zone it is waiting on.

docs.title: 💀 Orphaned
docs.text: Your partner failed that zone's encounter, so the other half is never coming. The Pokémon that was waiting dies.

docs.title: Signing
docs.text:
Right-click a player and pick Soul Link from Cobblemon's interaction wheel, next to Trade and Duel — or type /nuzlocke soullink link <player>.

Being offered a link is a screen you have to answer: Accept or Decline, no escape key, and it comes back if you die or log out while it is open. Agreeing to a Soul Link means agreeing that somebody else's mistakes can end your run, so it is not a line of chat that scrolls away.

Signing binds what you already own, matched up by zone on the spot. Anything caught somewhere your partner has not been simply waits.

docs.title: Bringing in a third and a fourth
docs.text: A contract can be extended at any time. Whoever joins binds into every zone they have already caught in, and the binds the others had already formed stay exactly as they were — nobody loses their team because somebody else signed.

docs.title: When it goes wrong
docs.text:
• Shared death — a linked Pokémon dies and every soulmate dies with it, even if its owner is offline. They meet the news on their next login.
  • No lone combat — a bound Pokémon stays in its ball unless its partners are in their owners' active parties, and those owners are online.
  • One last chance — being wiped out by your partner's loss is not instantly a Game Over. With zones still left to catch in, you may travel and try one more encounter. Land it and the run continues; fail it and it ends.
  • Starting over — /pokemonrestart takes you out of the contract. Your Pokémon leave every bind they were in and the others keep theirs; a bind left with only one member dissolves, so its Pokémon is free rather than pending.

docs.title: The Soul Link log
docs.text:
While you are in a link, the I key opens the link's log instead of your own. It is the same screen with the truth added:

It shows Why it matters Every member's zones, labelled with whose they are one member spending a zone changes what the others can still do Your partner's Pokémon in full species, nickname, and whether it is alive, dead or gone Which binds are waiting those are the Pokémon that cannot battle yet Who is on a Gym Leader Challenge, and on what type what your partner is even allowed to use

Partners who are offline still appear, showing the last state the run recorded.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Option Default What it does enable_soul_link on master toggle for the whole system soul_link_max_players 4 how many players one contract may hold (2–4) soul_link_request_seconds 120 how long an offer stays open, 15–600 seconds prevent_lone_combat on a bound Pokémon needs its partners active to be sent out

Soul Link sits on top of the Hardcore Nuzlocke rules — set both up from the same NUZLOCKE tab at world creation, or later with /nuzlocke set.
